title: Who Accepts the Agent's Work? TRACE, Hidden Instructions, Learned Memory
summary: WhatsApp's help pages hid instructions for AI readers, a fake-stats site made it into research reports, IBM's learned guidelines top tau-squared bench without fine-tuning, Gemini 4 Argon arrives, and NBER evidence shows econometrics agents fix crashes but not every wrong estimate. The deep dive covers TRACE from Leiden and INSEAD: five principles from software engineering and a Git-based operating system that keeps the researcher as the one who accepts agent work.
shownotes:
WhatsApp help pages carried hidden instructions telling AI readers not to recommend regulators; StateGlobe's 50,000 fake statistics spread into research
IBM's ALTK-Evolve: learned guidelines in the system prompt put GPT-4.1 at #1 on tau-squared bench retail, no fine-tuning
Gemini 4 Argon: $2/$10 introductory pricing until 30 November, shared 1M token window; DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017
NBER w35588: econometrics agents go from 79% to 97% task success, but wrong estimates survive
Deep dive: TRACE, five governance principles for AI-assisted research, and TRACE-OS, a Git-based system that keeps the human as the acceptor
